entries.title: Interactive reference by @RyanSael
entries.author: RyanSael
entries.prompt_text: Explain how camera focus works by building an interactive lens lab in one HTML file with three.js. Show a lens barrel with glass elements and a focus ring the viewer can turn; as it turns, the elements slide and a sharp focal plane moves through a small scene with objects at different depths. Draw the light rays converging, add live readouts for focus distance and aperture, and blur what is out of focus. Make it feel like a premium product lab.

entries.title: Interactive reference by @xikhar
entries.author: xikhar
entries.prompt_text: Build a third-person web-swinging game that runs in the browser with three.js. Generate a coastal city of tall procedural skyscrapers along a bay and an original masked hero who fires grapple lines to swing between towers, runs up walls and perches on spires. Model and rig the hero in Blender through Python, use generated images for facade and water textures, and add momentum-based swing physics, a chase camera, distance fog and a minimap. Keep it at 60 fps and record a two-minute play-through.

entries.title: Interactive reference by @Stefan_3D_AI
entries.author: Stefan_3D_AI
entries.prompt_text: Make a playable slice of a classic fantasy MMORPG in Unity, using Blender scripting and the image, 3D-model and music generation APIs I provide ({ASSET_APIS}) for assets. Open on a character creator (race, skin, hair style and color, name field, randomize button, rotating hero on a moonlit stage), then load a sunny farmland zone with wheat fields, a windmill and a lighthouse. Add third-person controls, a spell hotbar, a few quests and enemies, and an original score. Playtest it yourself and record a 1920×1080 gameplay capture.

entries.title: Interactive reference by @victormustar
entries.author: victormustar
entries.prompt_text: Engineer a {OBJECT} that can be built from genuine LEGO elements, then present it as a 1080×1080 build animation in three.js. Pick real part IDs, check that every stud connects, nothing overlaps and the model balances, and split the build into numbered steps. Show the pieces dropping in step by step over a pale sky-blue backdrop with soft contact shadows while the camera slowly orbits, and end on the finished model turning. Render frames with headless Chrome, encode with ffmpeg at 30 fps, and export a parts list.

entries.title: Interactive reference by @konstantinsaifo
entries.author: konstantinsaifo
entries.prompt_text: Using three.js in a single self-contained web page, build a browser lab that shows how a full-flow staged-combustion methane rocket engine works. Model the engine on a test stand with cutaway and exploded views, and animate color-coded liquid oxygen and methane as they pass through the two turbopumps, preburners and injector into the chamber. Add a throttle slider that changes plume length and brightness, an altitude switch from sea level to vacuum that reshapes the exhaust and its Mach diamonds, and short captions explaining each part.

entries.title: Interactive reference by @dangreenheck
entries.author: dangreenheck
entries.prompt_text: Construct a real-time tropical island in three.js that holds 60 fps at 1440p. Shape terrain with beaches, a jungle interior, a wooden dock and a village of huts, and scatter instanced palms and plants that bend in the wind. Bring it to life with seabirds that circle and dive, crabs that dash away and dig in as the camera nears, fish schools and a whale offshore, fluttering flags and lanterns, and a day-to-night cycle with glowing dock lights. Add a free camera that can pull back over the whole island.

entries.title: Interactive reference by @JaydenDavisNC
entries.author: JaydenDavisNC
entries.prompt_text: Code a third-person ink turf-war game for the browser in three.js. Two squads of four, lime against magenta, get three minutes to paint as much of a plaza arena as they can: players fire ink, dive into their own color to swim fast and reload, and lob splat bombs, with bots filling empty slots. Add a pause menu that lists controls and the roster, a coverage tally at the end, chunky toon shading and splashy synthesized sound, then record two minutes of play at 3840×2160.

entries.author: MatoToushi
entries.prompt_text: Design an interactive last-train map of {CITY} as a single HTML page using SVG and D3. Draw the rail network in each line's official color on a pale schematic base, with a sidebar listing every line and its final departure. A timeline from 21:30 to 01:30 has play and scrub controls; as the clock advances, trains glide along the tracks and each line greys out once its last service has gone. Include weekday and holiday timetables, light and dark themes, and smooth zoom.

entries.title: Interactive reference by @soyukke_game
entries.author: soyukke_game
entries.prompt_text: Make a tongue-in-cheek 3D arcade game that turns the trolley problem into pure strategy. The player rides a train down low-poly tracks across a green plain; before every fork, the left and right routes preview what waits on them and the damage a collision would cause, and yanking a big lever picks the branch. Carriages double as spendable power-ups, alongside HP and gold counters. Build it with three.js in one HTML file, with arrow-key and click controls and Web Audio sound, at 1280×720.

entries.title: Interactive reference by @The_Alex
entries.author: The_Alex
entries.prompt_text: Craft a grim souls-like action game that runs in the browser with three.js. Open on a cinematic title screen: a ruined fortress in darkness, an ember-glowing emblem and a serif title you invent. Gameplay follows a lone knight in third person through stone courtyards, with stamina-limited rolls, light and heavy sword attacks, bonfire checkpoints and a punishing boss. Use heavy fog, flickering torchlight, desaturated colors and Web Audio for clashing steel and low drones, then capture two minutes of play at 3840×2160.

entries.prompt_text: Program a 'touch grass' simulator in a single HTML file with three.js. Add rolling hills, a lone tree, a soft sky and distance fog, plus a key to crouch and run your fingers through the grass. Show an FPS counter, keep it smooth on a laptop, and record a 20-second walkthrough at 1920×1080.

entries.prompt_text: Recreate a notorious early-metaverse screenshot as a 10-second 3D shot in three.js, shown side by side with {REFERENCE_IMAGE} at 1080×1080. entries.title: Interactive reference by @MengTo
entries.author: MengTo
entries.prompt_text: Craft an explorable three.js river journey in a single HTML file, with a painted, cinematic look instead of photorealism: a small wooden boat is poled upstream through a Japanese valley in cherry-blossom season, past an arched red bridge, a hillside temple and pagoda, and stone lanterns. Put most effort into the water, with mirror reflections, foam around rocks and a V-shaped wake. Cycle through dawn, a thunderstorm, golden hour and a moonlit night, let an autopilot steer until WASD takes over, and synthesize river and rain sounds.

entries.prompt_text: Working only in Blender through its Python API, with every mesh, material and light made procedurally, build a fairy-tale castle on a still lake at night: clustered towers with pointed roofs, warm glowing windows, a starry sky, layered mountain silhouettes and a mirror reflection in the water. entries.prompt_text: In Roblox Studio, script an anime platform fighter in the spirit of Smash Bros with Luau, pulling arenas and props from the free Toolbox. entries.title: Interactive reference by @vib3coded

entries.prompt_text: Put a squishable watermelon-slice gummy in the browser as one HTML file on native WebGPU with WGSL. Give the wedge jelly-like red flesh, a whitish band, a striped rind and seeds that ride along as it deforms. Drive it with an XPBD soft-body solver on a tetrahedral mesh so any spot can be pinched, pulled and twisted, then jiggles back to rest. Light it like candy product photography on a pale backdrop, with refraction, rim glow and soft shadows, and add sliders for firmness and damping.

entries.title: Interactive reference by @gmi_cloud
entries.author: gmi_cloud
entries.prompt_text: Let the viewer wander an anime-style Japanese suburb at the height of cherry blossom season, built as a three.js web scene. Lay out narrow streets with painted road markings and kanji, utility poles strung with sagging power lines, two-storey houses, vending machines, a small bus and rows of sakura shedding petals that drift and pile up on the asphalt. Aim for the look of a hand-painted anime background with soft sky gradients and toon lighting, add WASD walking, and record a 60-second camera tour at 1920×1080.
